init.title: EZVIZ HP7 / CP7 options
init.description: Settings for this doorbell. Each option explains itself below it; the advanced section can usually be left as is.

data_description.monitor_serial: Enter the indoor monitor serial number (or several, separated by commas, for the HP7 two-family setup) to expose a dedicated switch per monitor. Empty = no monitor.

data_description.verification_code: The 6 letters on the device label. May be needed for log-in and/or to decrypt the video, depending on the mode.
data_description.encryption_key: Only if you changed the video encryption password in the EZVIZ app. Leave empty otherwise.
data_description.stream_quality: Applicable only to local playback via ports 9010/9020. When port 8000 is used, both video qualities will be available as separate video entities. Ignored by the Cloud source.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Relay and troubleshooting settings. Leave as they are unless you need them.

data_description.relay_bind: 127.0.0.1 = this host only (safe). 0.0.0.0 exposes the raw stream, WITHOUT authentication, to other hosts such as Frigate: trusted networks only, and it needs a fixed port.
data_description.aggressive_mpegts: Turn on only if the logs show 'Immediate exit requested'.
data_description.diagnostic_dumps: Writes two .bin files in /config with the start of the stream, for reporting a video problem. Leave off in normal use.

monitor_owner.name: Monitor owner account
monitor_owner.description: Only needed if this entry logs in with an account the monitor is shared with: such an account can't change the monitor's ring settings. Enter the monitor owner's account here. It is used only for those settings.

error.owner_auth: Could not log in with the monitor owner account. Check the e-mail and password (same region as this entry).
error.owner_mfa: The monitor owner account asks for a verification code at login, which this option does not support yet.
error.owner_password_missing: Enter the monitor owner account password.

hevc_webrtc.title: HEVC live view on WebRTC mode
hevc_webrtc.description:
Doorbell {serial} streams HEVC/H.265, but Stream mode is set to WebRTC. Browsers can't show HEVC over WebRTC and go2rtc must transcode, which fails on weak hosts (grey screen or 'connection refused').

Open Configure on the integration and set Stream mode to 'mjpeg' (codec-agnostic, no go2rtc), then Reload. Alternatively, to keep WebRTC, set Video codec to 'hevc' to transcode to H.264.

stream_encrypted.title: Device is encrypting the video stream
stream_encrypted.description:
Doorbell {serial} is scrambling the video stream (Image/Video Encryption is on). The container stays readable but the payloads are scrambled, so ffmpeg cannot decode and the live view stays black.

Open the EZVIZ app → the device → Settings → **Image/Video Encryption** and turn it off (it asks for the 6-letter device code). Note: a firmware or app update can silently re-enable it.

confirm.title: Enter the code EZVIZ e-mailed you
confirm.description:
Doorbell {serial} encrypts its video, and EZVIZ has just e-mailed a 4-digit security code (subject "[Device Encryption] Security Code") to your account address. That code unlocks the stream, and it expires after about 30 minutes.

Enter it below. Do **not** use the 6-character code printed on the device label — this firmware rejects it. Submitting an empty field asks EZVIZ for a fresh code.

error.invalid_code: EZVIZ did not accept that code. It has probably expired — submit an empty field to have a new one sent.
error.resent: A new code has been sent. Check your e-mail and enter it here.

abort.no_device: That doorbell is no longer set up in Home Assistant.

channel99_unavailable.title: Doorbell calls via polling only ({serial})
channel99_unavailable.description:
Home Assistant could not use EZVIZ's "channel 99" push for {serial} ({reason}). Channel 99 is the link the mobile app gets doorbell calls on; without it, unlocks still arrive by the regular push but rings are only seen by polling, up to 15 s late.

Common causes: the account asks for a verification code when logging in from a new phone, or the password changed. Log in to the EZVIZ app with this account once, then reload the integration. It is retried automatically every few hours.

confirm.title: Verification code needed for {serial}
confirm.description:
The stream source is "Local, port 8000 of the device", which logs in to the device with the verification code: the 6 letters on the device label. No code is configured, so the live view cannot start.

Enter the code below. Home Assistant checks it by logging in to the device on port 8000 before saving it. You can also enter it later in Configure → Live video → Verification code.

error.cannot_login: Home Assistant could not log in to the device on port 8000 with this code. Check the 6 letters on the device label, and that Home Assistant is on the same LAN as the doorbell.
error.invalid_code: The device refused this code. Check the 6 letters on the device label.

abort.no_device: That doorbell is no longer set up in Home Assistant.

confirm.title: Verification code rejected by {serial}
confirm.description:
The device refused the log-in on port 8000 with the configured verification code, so the live view cannot start. To avoid locking the device, Home Assistant does not try that code again until it is changed.

Enter the code below: the 6 letters on the device label. Home Assistant checks it by logging in to the device on port 8000 before saving it. You can also change it in Configure → Live video → Verification code.

error.cannot_login: Home Assistant could not log in to the device on port 8000 with this code. Check the 6 letters on the device label, and that Home Assistant is on the same LAN as the doorbell.
error.invalid_code: The device refused this code. Check the 6 letters on the device label.

abort.no_device: That doorbell is no longer set up in Home Assistant.

cloud_offline.title: EZVIZ cannot be reached
cloud_offline.description: {title} started without the EZVIZ cloud. Only the live video over the local network (port 8000) works, with the IP address and key stored the last time the cloud answered. Events, unlocking, the hang-up button and the settings come back by themselves: the login is tried again every 5 minutes and the integration reloads when EZVIZ answers.

unlock_door_failed.message: Unlocking the door failed. Check the EZVIZ cloud connection; the Home Assistant log has the reason.

unlock_gate_failed.message: Unlocking the gate failed. Check the EZVIZ cloud connection; the Home Assistant log has the reason.

hang_up_failed.message: Hanging up the doorbell call failed. Check the EZVIZ cloud connection; the Home Assistant log has the reason.

options.local: Local, ports 9010/9020 of the device: HA must be on the same LAN as the doorbell. May still need a cloud API call to get the stream key. Fixes 'no live' on firmware that won't push to the cloud
options.local_sdk: Local, port 8000 of the device. HA must be on the same LAN as the doorbell. It doesn't need the cloud at all. On 4K doorbells it can do both high-res and low-res streams simultaneously. It also works on accounts the doorbell is only shared with.

options.sub: Sub: low-resolution substream, much lighter to decode. Use it if video lags on a weak host (e.g. Raspberry Pi)

options.auto: Auto (default): detects the codec and picks, H.264 → WebRTC, HEVC → MJPEG
options.webrtc: WebRTC: HA Stream/go2rtc, with audio and low latency. Some browsers may not show HEVC
options.mjpeg: MJPEG: one ffmpeg per viewer, works with any codec and several viewers, no audio

options.hevc: HEVC → H.264: with WebRTC, transcodes HEVC to H.264 (might not work well on low-power hosts). MJPEG decodes HEVC directly.
options.hevc_copy: HEVC passthrough: passes H.265 untouched, for low-power hosts, Frigate or Safari. With WebRTC, the browser must support HEVC; MJPEG decodes it on the host.
